findings.title: af-3's non-ASCII candidate filter cannot reach the `ß`/`SS` pairing the plan's own Goal promises and this repo reproduced on APFS
findings.evidence: docs/plan/AUDIT_2026_10_20.md:14 (Goal item 3) names `ß`/`SS` as a pairing that must be preserved, but :87 filters deletion candidates to `!rel.as_os_str().as_encoded_bytes().is_ascii()` and :90 probes `entry_identity` only "For each non-ASCII `unmatched_dest` entry". A destination entry spelled `bSS` is pure ASCII, so it is dropped from the candidate set and never identity-probed. DEVLOG.md:8 (2026-10-19 22:55:59Z) records the live reproduction: "A separate APFS reproduction with no source counterpart confirmed the release-notes pure-glob safety limitation for `*ß`/`bSS` … each mirror exited 0 while deleting one saved file and directory." AC-3 (docs/plan/AUDIT_2026_10_20.md:35) silently drops `ß`/`SS` from the tested pairs, listing only `Übung`/`übung`, `σ`/`ς` and NFC/NFD.
findings.predicted_failure: After af-3 lands and is ticked, `blit mirror` on APFS with source `bß` and destination `bSS` still plans and executes the deletion of the destination file and its directory — the exact data-loss class af-3 exists to close — while the plan, REVIEW.md and docs/STATE.md record the Unicode-pairing defect as closed. The same hole covers Goal item 3's "case-insensitive mounts": on Linux `CasefoldKey` is the exact `PathBuf` (crates/blit-core/src/mirror_planner.rs:67), so an ASCII case variant such as `Foo`/`foo` on a case-insensitive mount is neither folded in memory nor probed on disk.
findings.better_approach: Gate the identity pass on the directory rather than the name: build `candidate_parent_dirs` from directories that hold either a non-ASCII unmatched destination candidate or an unmatched non-ASCII source/shield path, then probe `entry_identity` for every unmatched destination candidate in those directories, ASCII or not. A pure-ASCII tree still contributes no candidate directory and performs zero syscalls, so the FAST constraint at :28 is preserved, while `bß`/`bSS` and Linux case-insensitive-mount pairs become reachable. Add `bß`/`bSS` to AC-3 and state explicitly whether ASCII case variants on case-insensitive mounts are in scope.

findings.title: r1's adopted af-1 anchor names a function that does not exist and lands the copy/mirror rule on the move-only entry point
findings.evidence: docs/plan/AUDIT_2026_10_20.md:135 records F2 as "Adopted: anchored `af-1` at … `run_local_transfer` (`crates/blit-cli/src/transfers/local.rs:53`)", and :61 instructs `validate_local_transfer_roots(&src, &dst, false)` there. crates/blit-cli/src/transfers/local.rs:53 is `run_local_transfer_deferred`, documented at :44 as "Same as [`run_local_transfer`] but for the MOVE verb"; copy and mirror enter through `run_local_transfer_quiet` (:21) from crates/blit-cli/src/transfers/mod.rs:378. `run_local_transfer` survives only in stale doc comments (crates/blit-cli/src/transfers/local.rs:20 and :44, crates/blit-cli/src/transfers/mod.rs:832).
findings.predicted_failure: Following the plan puts an `is_move: false` validation on the move path — where the plan's own rule returns `Ok(Some(rel))` instead of bailing for a destination nested inside the source — and leaves copy and mirror with no CLI-level check at all, so AC-1's copy/mirror clause is satisfied only by the core-level call inside `run_local_session`, after both prompts have already run. Since r1's F2 was specifically the finding that the af-1 anchors were fictional, adopting it with a second fictional anchor means the plan's Review history asserts a correction that was never verified.
findings.better_approach: Use the single post-`prepare_transfer_route` anchor described above. If per-function anchors are kept instead, name `run_local_transfer_quiet` (crates/blit-cli/src/transfers/local.rs:21) for copy/mirror with `is_move: false` and `run_local_transfer_deferred` (:53) with `is_move: true` for move, and fix the three stale `run_local_transfer` doc references while touching the file.

findings.title: A same-family review is recorded as a formal openreview acceptance against D-2026-10-07-4, with no decision recording the override
findings.evidence: REVIEW.md:341 and docs/plan/AUDIT_2026_10_20.md:133 both record "openreview claude (claude-opus-5[1m] @ max, competitive)" returning acceptable_with_changes for a Claude-authored plan, and docs/STATE.md's new queue entry repeats it. docs/DECISIONS.md:932 (D-2026-10-07-4) states "A review is never run by the model family that wrote the change — a Claude-authored change is never reviewed by Claude" and "Every formal `openreview` dispatches Codex", and docs/DECISIONS.md:950 confirms D-2026-10-07-4 "continue[s] to govern any future review dispatch". DEVLOG.md:16 (2026-10-19 20:40:00Z), one day earlier, classified the identical situation as "Advisory only, NOT a formal openreview verdict … under D-2026-10-07-4 Claude cannot formally review a change from its own family." The range adds no docs/DECISIONS.md entry recording the owner's override.
findings.predicted_failure: The plan enters the 1.0 queue under D-2026-10-19-2 carrying an acceptance stamp the governance forbids, so a later agent reading REVIEW.md treats af-1..af-5 as independently vetted and skips the Codex dispatch D-2026-10-07-4 requires — which matters here because the same-family review passed through two anchor errors and an unreachable Unicode gate. The row also becomes citable precedent that `openreview claude` is a valid formal dispatch, while docs/DECISIONS.md still says the opposite, leaving the repo's memory self-contradictory on a load-bearing rule.
findings.better_approach: Relabel the row and the plan's Review history as an advisory second read, exactly as DEVLOG.md:16 did, keeping its four findings as candidate findings rather than an acceptance verdict; or re-dispatch the plan review to Codex per D-2026-10-07-4 on the owner's per-invocation approval (D-2026-07-23-7). If the owner intends the override to stand as policy, record it in docs/DECISIONS.md naming D-2026-10-07-4 as the superseded text, so one canonical location holds the rule.

findings.title: Acceptance recorded on an artifact whose own envelope shows both allowlisted capability commands denied, with no event stream retained
findings.evidence: .review/results/audit-2026-10-20-plan-r1.claude.json:1 — the payload asserts `"capability_ok":true` while its `permission_denials` array holds exactly two Bash entries, `rtk git diff --check c1778a92..dc4fb378` and `bash scripts/agent/check-docs.sh`, i.e. both of the allowlisted check commands the capability proof names. .agents/playbooks/openreview.md:135-138 defines `capability_ok` as "the folded-in transport proof … the reviewer sets it only after reading a repo file and running one allowlisted command in the same shot", and :128-134 makes acceptance fail-closed and explicitly the orchestrator's computation, not the reviewer's. No `.events.jsonl` was retained next to the result, unlike the codex rows at REVIEW.md:342, so nothing in the repo can show whether a third, permitted attempt succeeded.
findings.predicted_failure: The single acceptance record for this plan is unauditable on the one axis it exists to prove. If no allowlisted command ran, the four findings were produced without the transport the playbook requires and the orchestrator recorded an accepted verdict the fail-closed rule says it should have rejected; either way a future reader cannot distinguish the two, and the same pattern will repeat on the next dispatch because nothing in the record flags it.
findings.better_approach: Annotate the REVIEW.md row with the two denials and name the allowlisted command that actually ran; if none did, treat the dispatch as not-accepted per the fail-closed rule and re-run it. For every formal dispatch, run the harness in JSON event-stream mode with stdin closed and commit the raw event log beside the result, as the codex rows already do, so capability and heartbeat claims are checkable after the fact.

findings.title: af-1's `canonical_target_path` collapses `..` before canonicalizing and duplicates the walk af-4 is editing
findings.evidence: docs/plan/AUDIT_2026_10_20.md:50-51 specifies "Normalize `path` lexically via `std::path::absolute(path)` and collapse `.` / `..` components so relative forms … become clean absolute paths before touching the filesystem", then walk to the deepest existing ancestor, canonicalize it and re-append the tail. `std::path::absolute` deliberately preserves `..` on Unix precisely because a preceding component may be a symlink, so the collapse has to be done by hand and discards that information before `canonicalize` ever sees it. The deepest-existing-ancestor walk already exists at crates/blit-core/src/path_safety.rs:347-370 (`canonical_dest_root`) and inside `verify_contained` (:274-314) — the same file and functions af-4 modifies at docs/plan/AUDIT_2026_10_20.md:101-103.
findings.predicted_failure: For a path whose `..` follows a symlinked component — `blit copy /a/dir /a/dir/sub/link/..` where `link -> /elsewhere` — the lexical collapse yields `/a/dir/sub`, so the pair is judged nested when the real destination is `/elsewhere`'s parent, and af-2's pruning excludes a subtree the user asked to copy (or, with af-1's move rule, a legitimate move is refused). AC-2's "symlinked ancestor" clause is then met only for symlinks not followed by `..`. Separately, two copies of the ancestor walk drift the moment af-4 adds its `Component::ParentDir` rejection to only one of them.
findings.better_approach: Make the path absolute without collapsing `..`, let `std::fs::canonicalize` resolve both symlinks and `..` over the existing prefix, and handle only `..` that survives in the non-existent tail (reject it, or resolve it lexically there, and say which). Export the deepest-existing-ancestor walk from crates/blit-core/src/path_safety.rs as a shared helper and have af-1's `canonical_target_path` and af-4's hardened `canonical_dest_root` both build on it, so the containment semantics have one canonical location.
